title: Construction and Use of an Electrical Stimulation Chamber for Enhancing Osteogenic Differentiation in Mesenchymal Stem/Stromal Cells In Vitro
protocol: Construct the electrical stimulation cell culture chamber using two lids of standard 6-well cell culture plates.
Drill twelve holes, each with a diameter of ~1 mm, near the outer edge of each well in the lids (25 mm apart).
Cut twelve lengths of platinum wire, each 5 cm long.
Bend each platinum wire into an L-shape, leaving one end 3 cm long and the other 2 cm.
Insert the longer (3 cm) bent end of each platinum wire into a drilled hole from inside to out, leaving 1–2 mm protruding from the outside.
Secure the platinum wires in place with superconductive glue.
Allow the superconductive glue to dry for around 6 hours.
Solder the tips of all six platinum wires protruding from the lids to one of the silver-coated wires.
Solder the remaining six platinum wires to the other silver-coated wire.
Add LEDs in the circuit between each of the six anode-cathode platinum electrode pairs.
Place a piece of black insulation tape under each LED to prevent exposing cells to light.
Glue the wire terminal block connector to the top left corner of the 6-well plate lid.
Connect both silver-coated wires to the input terminals of the wire connector.
Cut out a 20 mm x 20 mm section from the top left corner of a second 6-well plate lid.
Cover the first lid, equipped with electrodes, with the second lid and tape them together.
Apply a 3–5 mm layer of silicone adhesive coating to improve bonding (optional).
Allow the silicone adhesive to dry for 12 hours before assembling the lids.
Connect one end of two standard insulated copper wires to the output terminals of the wire connector.
Attach the other ends of the copper wires to banana male connectors.
Turn on the power supply by pressing the ON/OFF button on the front panel.
Activate channel 1 by pressing button 1.
Press button Nr. 4 (V-set) to set the voltage.
Press buttons 2, . and 5 to set the load output at 2.5 V.
Ensure that the load output of 2.5 V corresponds to an EStim of 100 mV/mm according to the given equation.
Purchase commercially available rat MSCs and store them in liquid nitrogen until needed.
Remove one vial of MSCs from liquid nitrogen storage, quickly thawing it in a 37°C water bath within 1 minute.
Transfer the vial content into a 50 mL falcon tube under sterile conditions.
Add 9 mL of normal medium (DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin/streptomycin) prewarmed to 37°C to the cells in the falcon tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 x g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant under sterile conditions in a laminar flow hood.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 12 mL of normal medium prewarmed to 37°C.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a T-75 cell culture flask.
Culture the cells at 37°C, 5% CO₂, and 5% O₂ until they reach an 80%-90% confluence over 3–5 days.
Passage the cultured cells when they are confluent.
Retrieve cells when they reach an 80%-90% confluence.
Aspirate cell culture medium.
Wash twice with 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Add 5 mL of 1x cell detachment solution to the cells.
Return the plate to the incubator for 5 minutes.
Add an equal amount of culture medium to inactivate the detachment solution.
Collect detached cells in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Spin the collected cells at 300 x g for 5 minutes.
Discard the medium and resuspend cells in 1 mL of fresh normal medium.
Assess the number of viable cells with trypan blue stain.
Seed 1 x 10^6 cells in a new T-75 flask with 12 mL of prewarmed NM.
Culture the cells at 37 °C, 5 % CO2, 5 % O2 until they reach an 80%-90% confluence.
Seed 9 x 10^4 cells in 3 mL of NM in each well of a 6-well culture plate.
Incubate the cells for 1 day at 37 °C, 5 % CO2, 5 % O2.
Aspirate the culture medium from the wells.
Apply 3 mL of osteogenic differentiation medium (OM) to each well.
Place the 6-well plate with cells in the incubator.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5% CO2, 5% O2.
Sterilize the electrodes in a 70% ethanol solution for 30 min.
Dry the electrodes under UV light in a safety cabinet for 30 min.
Cover the 6-well plate containing cultured MSCs with the lid equipped with sterilized electrodes.
Submerge the electrodes completely in medium (add more if necessary).
Transfer the covered 6-well plate to the incubator and connect it to the power supply.
Set the power supply to a 2.5 V load output.
Treat the cells with EStim for 1 hour.
Disconnect the power supply after treatment.
Remove the EStim chamber from the incubator under sterile conditions.
Exchange the lid equipped with electrodes with a standard 6-well plate lid.
Return the cells to the incubator and leave them overnight.
Clean the electrodes first with PBS, then with 70% ethanol solution.
Use fine sandpaper to clean corrosion products from the electrode surface.
Repeat steps 3.1–3.5 for 6 consecutive days.
On day 4, prior to applying EStim, change the culture medium by aspirating 1.5 mL and replacing it with prewarmed fresh OM under sterile conditions.
Maintain cells in culture after applying EStim for an additional 7 days.
Exchange the medium every 3–4 days during this period.
Analyze cell morphology changes under a microscope.
Measure calcium deposition to assess the effect of EStim on MSC osteogenic differentiation.
Measure alkaline phosphatase activity to assess the effect of EStim on MSC osteogenic differentiation.
Measure osteogenic marker gene expression to assess the effect of EStim on MSC osteogenic differentiation.
